_note: Hand-authored contract layer (rms-design-system-engine) — COMMIT this file. It holds decisions only (Figma->code bindings, semantics, notes), never captured DS values, so it is safe to share and applies in CI. The generated contracts/ + tokens.json are local, gitignored views built from this + the Figma snapshots. Resolve a prop rename or slot by adding, under a component: "bindings": { "<figmaProp>": { "attribute": "codeName" } }  or  { "slot": "slotName" }. Optional agent guidance per component: "whenNotToUse" (string), "useInstead" (string or list), "neverCombineWith" (list of component names). Optional decision status: "status" (current | deprecated | experimental), "supersededBy" (the component that won), "since", "rationale" (the why).

whenToUse: Use it for each row of a list a person picks from to open or select an item (a token, a component, a setting), rows stacked one under another.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a row that only shows information and does nothing when clicked: use listItem.
Do not use it for the items of a flyout menu: use overflowList inside an overflow.
limitations: It is a fixed 40px tall and its title stays on one line.
Its action button and its arrow show only while the row is hovered, focused or selected, and a selected row hides its action button.
doDont: Do: use one row per item a person picks, stacked one under another.
Don't: use it for a row that does nothing when clicked: use listItem.

whenToUse: Use it for each token or component in a map of what uses what (Impact Atlas), selectable, with its type icon and name.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for the rows of an ordinary list: use buttonList or listItem.
mistakes: Fading the nodes not selected with opacity: use has-selection on their container, which draws them with the disabled tokens and keeps them usable.
limitations: It is a fixed 40px tall.
Its Disabled state takes no clicks; its receded and external looks reuse the disabled tokens but stay clickable.
doDont: Do: recede the nodes not selected with has-selection on their container.
Don't: fade nodes with opacity.

whenToUse: Use it to switch between two to four views or modes of the same content, always in view (Tokens and Components, Colors and Export).
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a choice in a form that is submitted later: use radioButtonGroup.
Do not use it for many options: use an overflow menu.
mistakes: Building it by hand instead of with createSegmentedControl: the sliding pill that marks the selected segment is not set up.
limitations: Its segments share its width evenly, as wide as the widest; with full-width it fills its row.
A segment too narrow for its icon and label hides its label.
doDont: Do: make it with createSegmentedControl, for two to four views of the same content.
Don't: use it for many options or for a choice in a form.

whenToUse: Use it to tag an item with a short status or severity next to its name (High, Low, Clipped, Truncated).
whenNotToUse: Do not use it as a button or a link: it takes no clicks.
Do not use it to mark a problem on a preview: use highlight, with a highlightSelector over the spot.
mistakes: Saying the status with its colour alone: its label must say it in words, so keep Show Label on unless the same words are beside it.
limitations: Its label stays on one line: keep it to one or two words.
It has four tones only (negative, warning, positive, neutral); each one uses its own badge tokens.
doDont: Do: say the status in one or two words beside the item's name.
Don't: use it as a button or link, or say the status by its colour alone.

whenToUse: Use it for a short value a person types: a search, a name, a number, with optional labels before and after the value and optional icons.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it to step a number through a range: use buttonStepper.
Do not use it to choose among a few known options: use segmentedControl, radioButtonGroup or checkBoxGroup.
mistakes: A field with no visible label and no aria-label: nothing names it to a screen reader.
limitations: It is one line, 24px tall: there is no multi-line form.
Disabled or read-only, it loses its fill and takes no pointer events.
doDont: Do: give it a visible label or an aria-label.
Don't: use it to step a number through a range: use buttonStepper.

whenToUse: Use it to confirm that something finished (showToast) or to report that it failed (showError): a short message that goes away on its own.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for something still in progress: use loader (showProgress).
Do not use it for a question or a choice: use modal.
mistakes: Reporting a failure in an inline banner instead: every plugin reports failures with showError.
limitations: Its message stays on one line: keep it short.
It closes after 5 seconds, 8 for an error; the time stops while the pointer or the focus is on it.
doDont: Do: confirm with showToast and report a failure with showError.
Don't: use it for something still in progress: use loader.

whenToUse: Use it for the actions that sit inside a row, a bar or a loader (focus on canvas, cancel), where a bordered button would be too loud.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for the main action of a view: use buttonPrimary.
Do not use it for a remove or clear icon right beside a value: use buttonQuaternary.
mistakes: An icon-only one with no data-tip or aria-label: nothing names it to a screen reader.
limitations: It is 24px tall and its label stays on one line.
Disabled, it fades to 24% and takes no clicks or hover.
doDont: Do: use it for actions inside rows, bars and loaders.
Don't: leave an icon-only one without a data-tip or aria-label.

whenToUse: Use it to show a colour value as a small chip, beside its name, as in Tokens to Ink's tables.
Use Filled False (the hatched chip) when there is no colour to show.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it as a colour picker or a button: it takes no clicks.
mistakes: Showing it with no name for its colour: as an image, it needs an aria-label, or the colour's name beside it.
limitations: It is a fixed 24px square.
doDont: Do: name its colour with an aria-label or the name beside it.
Don't: use it as a button or a colour picker.

whenToUse: Use it for each choice in an overflow menu: an optional icon and a label.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it outside an overflow menu: use buttonList for a list on the page.
mistakes: An item with an icon and no words: nothing names it.
limitations: It is a fixed 32px tall, between 56px and 280px wide, and its label stays on one line.
doDont: Do: give every item words, with an optional icon before them.
Don't: use it outside an overflow menu: use buttonList.

whenToUse: Use it for the actions beside the main one, and for standalone actions that should stand out less than it (refresh, add, view on canvas, close a modal).
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for the one main action of a view: use buttonPrimary.
Do not use it for quiet actions inside rows and bars: use buttonTertiary.
mistakes: With Show Label off it shows only its icon, so nothing names it: give it a tip (data-tip, which the system makes its name) or an aria-label where it is used.
limitations: It is 24px tall and its label stays on one line.
Disabled, it fades to 24% and takes no clicks or hover.
doDont: Do: use it beside the main action, for actions that should stand out less.
Don't: use it for the one main action of a view: use buttonPrimary.

whenToUse: Use it for the smallest action right beside the thing it acts on, such as removing an output from a table row or clearing a field.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for an action a person must find at a glance: it shows no fill or border until hovered; use buttonSecondary.
mistakes: An icon-only one with no data-tip or aria-label: nothing names it to a screen reader.
limitations: Figma draws only its Default and Hover states: it has no disabled look of its own.
It is 24px tall and its label stays on one line.
doDont: Do: put it right beside what it removes or clears, with a data-tip or aria-label.
Don't: use it for an action a person must find at a glance.

whenToUse: Use it to title each section of a long list (affected components, a severity group), with an optional severity dot, a count and one action.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for the title of a view, a panel or a modal: it is a small heading for list sections.
Do not use it for a line with no name: use dividerLine.
mistakes: Leaving its background transparent: it stays at the top while its section scrolls, so it takes the colour of the surface it sits on, or the rows show through it.
limitations: It holds one action button at most, right after its title.
The system gives it heading level 2 when the product sets none.
doDont: Do: give it the surface colour it sits on, so rows do not show through it.
Don't: use it as the title of a view, a panel or a modal.

whenToUse: Use it for one option among several where only one can be chosen, inside a radioButtonGroup.
Its Current and Unselected states mark the steps of a stepper: the current step, and the ones not reached.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it when several options can be on at once: use checkBox.
Do not use it for two to four short options always in view in a toolbar: use segmentedControl.
mistakes: With Show Text off it has no words, so nothing names it: give it an aria-label, or aria-labelledby on the words that describe it, where it is used.
limitations: A choice cannot be undone to nothing chosen: once one radio is picked, one stays picked.
doDont: Do: give the radios of one choice the same name, inside a radioButtonGroup.
Don't: use it when several options can be on at once: use checkBox.

whenToUse: Use it for a side area of the plugin beside the main content, with a head (a control such as a segmentedControl) over content that scrolls.
Use Type Primary (elevation medium) for the main panel and Type Secondary (elevation low) for one that recedes; panel--resizable adds a handle to drag its width.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it to group a few settings inside a view: use card.
Do not use it for a short task to finish before going on: use modal.
mistakes: Adding a border to it: its surface colour alone sets it apart, as in Figma.
limitations: Only its main content scrolls; its head stays in place.
doDont: Do: put a control in its head and the content that scrolls in its main part.
Don't: give it a border: its surface sets it apart.

whenToUse: Use it at the edge of a view for what is selected and what can be done with it at once: its name and type, a badge, a count and a few buttons.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for the controls that act on the whole view (rescan, search, filters): use actionBar.
mistakes: Adding a divider on a wrapper around it: it draws its own top and bottom lines, which no-divider-top and no-divider-bottom turn off.
limitations: It is a fixed 48px tall and does not wrap.
doDont: Do: show what is selected and the actions on it.
Don't: put the controls for the whole view in it: use actionBar.

whenToUse: Use it for the row of controls that act on the whole view, right under the plugin's header: rescan, search, filters and the view's main actions.
Use its plain form (no background, no dividers) to give one centred control, such as a segmentedControl, the bar's breathing room.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for the actions of one item: they belong in that item's row (buttonList, listItem or table/row).
Do not use it for what is selected or counted at the edge of a view: that is statusBar.
mistakes: Adding a border or a divider on a wrapper around it: it draws its own top and bottom lines, which no-divider-top and no-divider-bottom turn off.
limitations: It wraps its controls onto another line when they do not fit; it never scrolls sideways.
It reaches the edges of its container by pulling out of the container's padding/l, so it goes directly in a view padded with padding/l.
doDont: Do: put the controls that act on the whole view in it, right under the header.
Don't: wrap it in a border or divider of your own: it draws its own lines.

whenToUse: Use it for a flyout menu that opens from a button and lists choices as overflowList rows, with an optional title.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for content that stays on the page: use card or panel.
Do not use it for a choice among two to four options always in view: use segmentedControl.
mistakes: Putting anything but overflowList rows (and its title) in it: the menu loses its row rhythm and its dividers.
limitations: The product places it and opens or closes it: it has no position of its own.
doDont: Do: fill it with overflowList rows only, with an optional title.
Don't: use it for content that stays on the page: use card or panel.

whenToUse: Use it for the one main action of a view, a modal or an empty state (Export, Scan, Add output).
whenNotToUse: Do not put two of them side by side: the other action is a buttonSecondary.
Do not use it for the actions inside rows, bars or loaders: use buttonTertiary.
mistakes: With Show Label off it shows only its icon, so nothing names it: give it a tip (data-tip, which the system makes its name) or an aria-label where it is used.
limitations: It is 24px tall and its label stays on one line.
Disabled, it fades to 16% and takes no clicks or hover.
doDont: Do: use one for the main action of a view or a modal.
Don't: put two side by side: the other action is a buttonSecondary.

whenToUse: Use it for the small help or info icon beside a label, a name or a setting, whose tooltip (data-tip) says more about it.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for an action: it only shows its tooltip; use buttonTertiary.
mistakes: Putting the only way to understand something in its tooltip when the words could be on the page.
limitations: Its icon changes with the feature (info, library), as Figma notes; its box is always the button height.
doDont: Do: put it beside the label it explains, with its words in data-tip.
Don't: use it for an action: use buttonTertiary.

whenToUse: It shows by itself for any element with a data-tip, on hover or keyboard focus: give the element a data-tip rather than drawing a tooltip.
whenNotToUse: Do not put controls or links in it: it holds text only.
Do not use it for something a person must read to go on: say it on the page.
mistakes: Adding a title attribute as well as a data-tip: the browser shows its own tooltip on top of the system's.
limitations: It is at most 240px wide and wraps its text.
There is one on the page, which every data-tip shares.
doDont: Do: give the element a data-tip and let the system show it.
Don't: put controls or links in it, or add a title attribute as well.

whenToUse: Use it for an option a person turns on or off on its own, independently of the others, usually inside a checkBoxGroup.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it when only one of the options can be chosen: use radioButton.
Do not use it for a setting that takes effect the moment it is changed: use switch.
mistakes: With Show Text off it has no words, so nothing names it: give it an aria-label, or aria-labelledby on the words that describe it, where it is used.
limitations: It has two states, unchecked and checked: there is no mixed state.
doDont: Do: use it for options that each turn on or off on their own.
Don't: use it when only one option can be chosen: use radioButton.

whenToUse: Use it while something takes time (a scan, an export), with a title saying what is happening, an optional description such as the time left, and an optional Cancel.
Show it with showProgress, which centres it in an overlay over the page, and remove it with dismissProgress.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it to confirm that something finished, or to report a failure: use toast (showToast, showError).
mistakes: Leaving it up after the work ends or fails: call dismissProgress on every way out.
limitations: Its title stays on one line.
It holds one action at most, a buttonTertiary.
doDont: Do: show it with showProgress and remove it with dismissProgress on every way out.
Don't: use it to say something finished or failed: use a toast.

whenToUse: Use it to put one label over several related checkBoxes that each turn on or off.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it when only one of the options can be chosen: use radioButtonGroup.
mistakes: Leaving its label out: the group is named by it, through aria-labelledby.
limitations: Its slot lays the checkboxes in one row, gap/xxxl apart, and does not wrap them onto a second line.
doDont: Do: give it a label that names what the checkboxes are for.
Don't: use it when only one option can be chosen: use radioButtonGroup.

whenToUse: Use it to put one label over the radioButtons of one choice, such as an export format.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it when several options can be on at once: use checkBoxGroup.
mistakes: Giving its radios different names: they stop being one choice, and arrow keys no longer move between them.
limitations: Its slot lays the radios in one row, gap/xxxl apart, and does not wrap them onto a second line.
doDont: Do: give it a label that names the choice.
Don't: give its radios different names.

whenToUse: Use it as the label that names a problem found on a preview (clipped, truncated, overflow), placed beside the highlightSelector that marks the spot.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it to tag an item in a list: use badge.
Do not use it to stress words in running text.
mistakes: Showing it without a highlightSelector: the person cannot tell which spot it names.
limitations: It is 24px tall and its label stays on one line.
It has one tone: the red of a problem.
doDont: Do: place it beside the highlightSelector that marks the spot it names.
Don't: use it to tag an item in a list: use badge.

whenToUse: Use it to mark the area of a problem over a preview, such as a text layer that is clipped; its Selected state marks the one the person pinned.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it to show which item of a list is selected: list rows have their own Selected state.
mistakes: Using it as the only sign of a problem: name it with a highlight, since its marker says nothing in words.
limitations: It draws a box only: the product sets its size and position over the preview.
It is decorative to a screen reader (Role: presentation): what it marks must be said elsewhere.
doDont: Do: name the problem it marks with a highlight beside it.
Don't: use it to show which row of a list is selected.

whenToUse: Use it to separate two groups of content in a list or a view with a thin line.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it as a section title: use dividerSection, which names the section.
Do not add one under a component that draws its own line (buttonList, overflowList, statusBar, actionBar, or one with Show Divider on).
mistakes: Drawing a border on a wrapper instead: the line no longer follows the dividerLine/border token.
limitations: It is horizontal only, one general/thickness tall.
doDont: Do: use it to separate two groups of content.
Don't: add one under a component that draws its own line.

whenToUse: Use it to change a number in steps within a known range, such as a scale or a zoom level.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for free text or a number with no range: use input.
Do not use it to choose among named options: use segmentedControl or radioButtonGroup.
mistakes: Building the minus and plus buttons by hand instead of calling initButtonStepper, or leaving out the field's role spinbutton with its aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow: the arrow keys and what a screen reader hears stop working.
limitations: Its field is a fixed 119px wide, with its value centred.
Its buttons turn off at each end of the range, and a typed value is brought back within the range when the field is left.
doDont: Do: drive it with initButtonStepper and give its field its range.
Don't: use it for a number with no range: use input.

whenToUse: Use it for each option of a segmentedControl: a label, an icon or both, with an optional number and status dot.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it on its own, outside a segmentedControl.
mistakes: With Show Label off it shows only its icon or number, so nothing names it: give it an aria-label where it is used.
limitations: Its label collapses when the segment is too narrow to show both its icon and its label.
A segment with nothing behind it (tab-empty) is dimmed and cannot be chosen.
doDont: Do: keep its label short, so it fits beside its icon.
Don't: use it outside a segmentedControl.

whenToUse: Use it for a short task or a choice that must be finished or dismissed before going on (export options, a check before running), opened with openModal and closed with closeModal.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a message that needs no answer: use toast.
Do not use it for content a person keeps open while working: use panel.
mistakes: Showing it by toggling its class instead of openModal: the focus is not moved into it, kept in it or returned to its opener, and Escape does not close it.
limitations: It is a fixed 320px wide; its height follows its content.
Its footer lays its buttons in one row, sharing the width.
doDont: Do: open it with openModal and close it with closeModal.
Don't: use it for a message that needs no answer: use a toast.

whenToUse: Use it in place of a list or a view's content when there is nothing to show (nothing selected, no results), saying why and what to do next.
Use Type Positive, with its check icon, when an empty result is good news, such as no issues found.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it to report a failure: use showError, which shows an error toast.
Do not use it while content is still loading: use loader.
mistakes: A title alone when the person needs to know what to do next: add its description, or its action button.
limitations: Its column is at most 260px wide and its text at most 200px; it centres itself in the area it fills.
doDont: Do: say why there is nothing to show and what to do next.
Don't: use it to report a failure: use showError.

whenToUse: Use it for each row of a list that shows information: an icon, a title, an optional description and one optional action, with a divider under it.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it when the whole row is what a person clicks to open or select something: use buttonList.
Do not use it for a row with a value and its outputs: use table/row.
mistakes: Mixing other elements in among the list items: the system makes their container a list only when it holds list items alone.
limitations: It holds one action at most, a buttonTertiary at the end of the row.
doDont: Do: put list items alone in their container, so it reads as a list.
Don't: use it when the whole row opens or selects something: use buttonList.

whenToUse: Use it to cover a view while something blocks it, with what is happening at its centre (a loader).
whenNotToUse: Do not use it behind a dialog: modal has its own overlay.
Do not use it to dim content that stays usable.
mistakes: Placing it in a container that is not positioned: it covers the nearest positioned ancestor, which may be the whole page.
limitations: It covers its container: its size comes from where it is placed, as Figma notes.
It is decorative to a screen reader: what it holds says what is happening.
doDont: Do: place it in a positioned container, with what is happening at its centre.
Don't: use it behind a modal, which has its own.

whenToUse: Use it to group related settings or one output into a bordered block within a view, with an optional title above its content.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a whole side area of the plugin: use panel.
Do not use it for one row of a list: use listItem or buttonList.
mistakes: Putting a card inside a card: the two borders sit one inside the other and the content loses its padding rhythm.
limitations: Its height follows its content.
It has no fill of its own: it shows the surface it sits on.
doDont: Do: group related settings or one output in it, with an optional title.
Don't: put a card inside a card.

whenToUse: Use it for a setting that takes effect the moment it is turned on or off (bleed, crop marks), with its description beside it, an optional tooltipButton and an optional input for its value.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for an option that only applies once a form is submitted: use checkBox.
mistakes: With Show Description off it has no words, so nothing names it: give it an aria-label, or aria-labelledby on the words that describe it, where it is used.
limitations: It is on or off: there is no third state.
Disabled, it fades to 40% and takes no clicks.
doDont: Do: use it for a setting that takes effect at once.
Don't: use it for an option that only applies once a form is submitted: use checkBox.

whenToUse: Use it for each row of a table that pairs a value (a swatch, its name and its value) with its outputs, as in Tokens to Ink's export tables.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a simple list of items: use listItem or buttonList.
mistakes: Mixing other elements in among the rows of a table: the system makes their container a table only when it holds rows alone.
limitations: A long name is cut with an ellipsis on one line: put the full name in its tooltipButton.
doDont: Do: put rows alone in their table, each with its value and its outputs.
Don't: use it for a simple list: use listItem or buttonList.
